title: Several units have blocked drains: give the strata plumber one clear incident report
seoTitle: Strata Blocked Drains: Coordinate a Useful Report
description: Several strata units have drainage symptoms? Coordinate locations, timing, access and authorisation for a Lower North Shore sewer assessment.
body:
Create a simple incident record

List the affected locations

Record unit numbers and fixtures, including any common-area drains. Keep residents’ descriptions in plain language: toilet rising, shower backing up or water appearing at an outdoor opening. Avoid turning a reported symptom into a diagnosis.

Record the sequence

Note when each report arrived and whether the issue is continuing. The first report may not identify the first point affected, but the timeline still helps. Include recent plumbing work or earlier incidents if the information is available.

Identify the access contact

Provide one person who can coordinate keys, gates and resident access. A plumber arriving without access to the relevant area may be unable to complete the intended investigation, even if the symptoms are well documented.

Keep residents’ immediate instructions consistent

Ask residents to stop using fixtures that are backing up or causing overflow. Keep people away from escaped wastewater and avoid repeated flushing as a test. Any chemicals already used should be reported to the plumber.

Do not ask residents to open shared service covers or enter restricted areas. The building contact should arrange safe access through the normal process. If immediate danger is present, use the appropriate emergency response rather than waiting for a routine appointment.

Agree on the investigation scope

Ask which access points and pipe sections will be assessed, and whether clearing is needed before inspection can be useful. Confirm who can approve a change in scope if the initial work reveals a separate problem.

The purpose is to establish what is happening in the relevant drainage path. A blockage affecting several units can suggest shared pipework, but the report should identify the actual findings rather than treating that suggestion as proof.

Request a report the committee can use

A useful report records the inspected location, obstruction or defect found, work completed and remaining limitations. Photos or footage should be tied to a location or explanation so a committee member can understand what they show.

Separate immediate clearing from any proposed permanent repair. Ask for the repair rationale, access requirements and restoration scope. That allows the owners corporation to consider a defined proposal instead of a broad recommendation to replace drains.

NSW’s strata repairs guidance explains responsibility for repairs in strata. Use the relevant plan and arrangements alongside the plumbing findings; do not allocate costs solely from the location of the first complaint.

Book through one coordinated contact

Our Lower North Shore sewer blockage service can assess the incident. Send the timeline and available previous reports when arranging the visit.

If the same manager also looks after a Northern Beaches property, Blocked Drains Northern Beaches offers a relevant regional contact. Keep each building’s reports and approval trail separate, even when the symptoms sound similar.

Give strata one evidence-based briefing

Compile a short shared timeline with unit numbers, fixtures and any overflow locations. Keep assumptions about ownership out of the symptom report. Ask the appointed plumber to identify inspected sections and remaining access needs. The strata contact can then compare those findings with the scheme's documents when arranging repairs and considering responsibility.
faqs: Does more than one affected unit prove a common-property fault?
It is useful evidence, but the affected pipe section and strata arrangements still need to be established.
Should every resident book a plumber?
A coordinated building response is usually more useful when a shared issue is suspected. Follow the building’s repair and emergency process.
Does a shared symptom prove the owners corporation pays?
No. Establish the affected component and check the strata plan, by-laws and applicable responsibility before allocating costs.
Who should coordinate access for a shared drain?
Use the building's nominated strata or property contact so access to units, inspection points and shared areas can be arranged together.
What should residents include in an incident report?
Include unit numbers, affected fixtures, times, overflow locations and recent work. Separate direct observations from assumptions about the cause.
Should each unit keep testing its plumbing?
No. Further use can worsen a shared overflow. Coordinate advice through the building contact while the affected system is assessed.
Could an upstairs discharge affect a lower unit?
Yes. Connected drainage can make a lower fixture show symptoms of a restriction elsewhere. Location of the backup does not prove fault ownership.
Can a plumber's report help clarify responsibility?
It can identify the section and observed defect. Legal responsibility still depends on the property documents and applicable arrangements.
What if tenants discover the problem first?
Notify the managing agent or building emergency contact promptly, provide the evidence and follow the property's repair process.
Does urgent attendance guarantee reimbursement?
No. Keep records and notify the responsible contact, but do not assume that authorising work establishes who must pay.
check: Three residents report symptoms on the same morning
Give the coordinating contact all three locations and times so one investigation can consider the shared drainage route.
imageAlt: Plumber handling drain-clearing equipment outside a residential apartment building
caption: Access and a clear incident report help a plumber investigate shared drainage.
introduction: When several units report drainage problems, give the coordinating plumber one clear record of the affected locations, timing and access arrangements. A possible shared blockage needs a building-level investigation, rather than separate assumptions based on whichever bathroom overflowed first. For a Lower North Shore strata manager or committee member, the immediate goal is to organise useful information and safe access. Deciding who pays comes after the relevant findings and property arrangements have been checked.
takeaways: Combine symptoms, timing and access details into one report.
Keep residents away from overflow and unnecessary testing.
Identify who approves work and receives the findings.
Separate urgent clearing from the later repair decision.

conclusion: One clear incident report helps a strata drain investigation. Bring symptoms, access and authorisation together, then keep urgent clearing separate from decisions about further repairs.

title: Sewage coming out of an outdoor drain? What to do before the plumber arrives
seoTitle: Outdoor Sewer Overflow: What to Do First
description: Wastewater escaping outdoors? Keep clear, stop contributing water use and prepare the details for an urgent Lower North Shore drain assessment.
body:
Make the area safe without entering it

Keep children, pets and visitors clear. Avoid walking through the water to take a closer photo or move stored items. If electrical equipment or outlets are wet, keep away and seek appropriate emergency help.

Photograph the situation only from a safe, dry position. A wide view showing the location is often more useful than a close-up taken beside the overflow. Note the time and whether the flow changes when water is used inside.

Stop adding to the problem

Pause use of fixtures that cause the overflow to increase. Do not repeatedly flush toilets or run taps to check whether the drain has cleared itself. Avoid adding drain chemicals or trying to wash the escaped wastewater towards another drain.

The NSW EPA’s stormwater management guidance explains the need to keep pollutants out of stormwater. Redirecting an overflow into a street drain is not a suitable clean-up strategy.

Give the booking contact four details

  1. The exact property address and location of the overflow.
  2. Whether the discharge is continuing and which fixtures appear involved.
  3. Whether anyone has already attempted clearing or added chemicals.
  4. Access instructions and the responsible property or strata contact.

If the property is a unit block, notify the strata contact promptly. If you rent, report it through the property’s urgent-repair process. Make clear that this is an active overflow rather than a routine slow-drain enquiry.

What needs to be established onsite?

The plumber needs to identify the affected drainage section and the likely obstruction or fault. The visible overflow point is not necessarily where the blockage sits. Access, pipe condition and the amount of retained wastewater can affect the investigation.

Ask what immediate work is proposed and how the result will be checked. If clearing restores flow but the underlying condition is uncertain, request that distinction in the report. It helps determine whether further inspection or repair is needed.

Keep clearing and clean-up separate in the scope

Restoring drainage does not automatically clean every affected surface or material. Ask what the plumbing visit includes and whether separate professional clean-up is needed. Do not assume a cleared pipe means the area is ready for normal use.

Document affected areas for the responsible property contact before disposal or restoration decisions are made. Keep the plumbing report and photographs together, particularly where more than one property or a common area is involved.

Our Lower North Shore sewer-drain service is the relevant point for the plumbing assessment. If the issue is at a separate Ryde property, The Ryde Plumber can help clarify the local service enquiry.

Separate immediate containment from the repair plan

Stop contributing wastewater, keep people away and report whether neighbouring properties or public assets are affected. Once the immediate situation is assessed, ask which section caused the overflow and what follow-up is justified. Cleaning contaminated surfaces is a separate concern; do not hose sewage into stormwater or assume restored flow makes the area safe.
faqs: Is an outdoor overflow always a private pipe problem?
No. The affected section needs to be established, and the relevant property or water-service contact may need to be involved.
Can I hose the area down once flow stops?
Ask for appropriate clean-up advice for the affected area. Do not move contamination into stormwater or assume all materials can be cleaned the same way.
What does gurgling in another fixture tell you?
It suggests connected drainage behaviour worth investigating. Sound alone cannot identify roots, a collapse or the exact restriction.
Should I use chemical cleaner before the visit?
Avoid adding chemicals to an overflowing or repeatedly blocked drain. Tell the plumber which products have already been used.
Can I keep using appliances on the affected drain?
Stop use that causes rising water or overflow. Ask what can remain in service once the connected drainage has been assessed.
Does restored flow mean the underlying fault is fixed?
No. Clearing removes an obstruction; a damaged joint, entry point or other defect may remain and need a separate decision.
When can a camera inspection help?
It can show accessible internal pipe condition once visibility allows. Standing water, debris and bends can limit what is seen.
What should a blocked-drain quote explain?
Ask about attendance, clearing method, access, inspection, reporting and what would require further approval. Repairs should have a defined scope.
Should I provide records of earlier drain clearing?
Yes. Dates, symptoms, footage and repair reports help compare recurrence with the earlier findings.
Can every drain be water-jetted?
No. Pipe size, material, condition and access affect equipment choice. The method should suit the assessed installation.
check: Keep clear, stop contributing fixture use and arrange urgent assessment with the exact overflow location and access details.
imageAlt: Plumber using drain equipment through an opening in a timber deck
caption: Company image illustrating this type of plumbing work.
introduction: If wastewater is overflowing from an outdoor drain, keep people away and stop using fixtures that add to the overflow. Arrange urgent plumbing assessment and explain where the water is escaping, whether it is still flowing and whether other properties appear affected. Do not treat it as ordinary rainwater because it is outside. The immediate job is to limit exposure and further discharge while the source and affected drainage section are identified.
takeaways: Keep people clear and stop contributing water use.
Report an active overflow clearly when calling.
Do not wash wastewater into another drain.
Confirm both the drainage outcome and the clean-up scope.

headings.label: Make the area safe without entering it
Stop adding to the problem
Give the booking contact four details
What needs to be established onsite?
Keep clearing and clean-up separate in the scope
Separate immediate containment from the repair plan

conclusion: An outdoor sewage overflow needs prompt reporting and a clear area around it. Stop contributing water use where possible and leave the drainage assessment and clean-up scope to the appropriate professionals.

title: CCTV drain inspection cost: what you should receive beyond a camera visit
seoTitle: CCTV Drain Inspection Cost: Report and Scope Checks
description: Compare CCTV drain inspection cost by access, preparation, coverage and reporting. Know what evidence to request on the Lower North Shore.
body:
Decide what you need to know

Are you investigating repeated blockages, checking a suspected defect or reviewing a section before proposed work? Tell the plumber the purpose of the inspection. The question affects the scope and the type of explanation you need afterwards.

Provide previous reports if available. An old finding can help identify the area of interest, but the current inspection should still state what was actually observed. Do not ask the new report to confirm an earlier assumption without checking it.

Compare four inclusions

Access and preparation

Ask which access point will be used and whether it is currently reachable. If the line is obstructed, clearing may be needed before useful footage can be obtained. Clarify whether that is included or separately quoted.

The inspected section

Ask where the inspection is intended to start and finish. A camera visit to one branch does not automatically cover every drain at the property. Where the route is uncertain, the quote should describe that limitation.

The evidence supplied

Confirm whether you will receive footage, still images, a written summary or a combination. Ask how any observed defect will be identified in relation to the property. A finding is more useful when the location can be understood.

Interpretation and next steps

The report should distinguish observed conditions from suspected causes. If a repair is recommended, ask how it relates to the evidence. If further work is needed to establish the condition, that should be stated plainly.

Understand what can limit the result

Retained water, deposits, tight bends or unavailable access can prevent a complete view. An inspection should not be described as comprehensive if relevant sections were not reached or visible. Ask for those limits in the handover.

Equally, a clear view of one section does not prove every connected pipe is sound. Keep the conclusion tied to the inspected area. That is especially useful when a report will be shared with an owner, committee or another contractor.

Avoid paying twice for missing information

Before booking, explain who will use the findings and what decision they need to make. A repair quote, maintenance plan and property-management report can require different detail. Agreeing the output early reduces misunderstandings later.

Our Lower North Shore CCTV inspection service is the relevant place to discuss the scope. If another property is on the Upper North Shore, Blocked Drains Upper North Shore provides a regional enquiry for that separate address.

For plumbing and draining work, the NSW trade-licence guidance helps you check the relevant credentials. Ask who will undertake and explain the inspection rather than choosing on price alone.

Compare the deliverables behind the camera price

Ask whether the quote includes necessary clearing, locating, saved footage and an explanation of the findings. Confirm the accessible length and how limitations will be recorded. A cheap camera attendance and a documented condition assessment may deliver different things, so compare what you will receive before comparing totals.
faqs: Is a camera inspection always possible before clearing?
No. An obstruction or retained water may limit visibility or access. Ask which sequence will produce a useful result.
Should I receive the footage?
Confirm that before booking. The agreed deliverables should state whether footage, images and a written explanation are included.
Can CCTV show every underground defect?
No. It shows what the camera can reach and see. Opaque water, obstructions, bends and access limits can leave sections unassessed.
Should the report identify the inspected length?
Yes. Ask for the start point, sections reached and any limitations so the findings are not mistaken for a whole-property clearance.
Is saved footage the same as an explanation?
No. Ask for a plain-English account of the observations, their location where established and any recommended next step.
Can a camera locate the pipe above ground?
Some inspections can include suitable locating equipment, but this is not automatic. Confirm whether locating is needed and included.
Does finding roots identify the responsible tree?
No. Roots visible in a pipe do not by themselves identify which tree they came from or establish responsibility.
Should repair be approved immediately after inspection?
Ask to understand the evidence, options and defined scope first. Urgent temporary action and a permanent repair can be separate decisions.
Can I use an old camera report for a new quote?
Share it with its date and location details. Changed symptoms or incomplete footage may require further inspection.
What should a completion inspection establish?
It should check the agreed accessible work area and explain remaining limitations. It should not be presented as a guarantee about unseen pipework.
check: The quote says CCTV inspection only
Ask which section, what preparation and which report or footage are included before accepting it.
imageAlt: Plumber feeding an inspection camera into an outdoor drain access point
caption: Company image illustrating this type of plumbing work.
introduction: A useful CCTV drain inspection should answer a defined question and explain what the camera could and could not show. When comparing cost, check the access, inspected section, clearing requirements and the report or footage included, not simply the time a camera is on site. For a Lower North Shore owner or property manager, that makes the result much easier to use. A video without a clear location or explanation may be difficult to turn into a repair decision.
takeaways: Define the question before booking the camera visit.
Compare preparation, coverage and reporting inclusions.
Ask for the location and limitations of each finding.
Connect repair recommendations to visible evidence.

Access and preparation

The evidence supplied
Interpretation and next steps
Understand what can limit the result
Avoid paying twice for missing information

conclusion: A useful camera inspection answers a defined question and explains what could actually be seen. Compare access, coverage and reporting, then connect any repair recommendation to the findings.

title: Ground-Floor Unit Gets the Backup: Could the Shared Sewer Be Blocked?
seoTitle: Ground-Floor Sewer Backup? Lower North Shore Drains
description: Sewer backup in a ground-floor unit? Learn why the lowest affected fixture may reveal a shared blockage and what to report on the Lower North Shore.
body:
Why the lowest fixture may show the problem first

Several units can discharge into connected pipework. If the outlet farther along is restricted, incoming water needs somewhere to collect. A low shower waste, toilet or other opening may show the backup before residents upstairs notice any symptoms.

That is a possible explanation rather than proof of a shared sewer blockage. The affected unit may also have a local branch fault. The plumber needs the layout, timing and accessible evidence to distinguish those situations. A ground-floor address alone does not establish which section has failed.

What residents should report straight away

Contact the strata manager, building manager or nominated emergency contact and describe the affected fixtures. Tenants should also notify their property manager or landlord. If sewage is escaping, say so clearly rather than reporting only that the drain is slow.

Stop using affected fixtures and keep people and pets out of the wet area. The building contact can coordinate advice to other residents if their water use may contribute. Do not go door to door making claims about who caused the blockage; the initial priority is limiting further discharge and arranging assessment.

Blocked drains in strata: separate the fault from responsibility

The NSW Government’s strata repair guidance explains the owners corporation’s responsibility for common-property repairs and how residents should report problems. The relevant pipe, strata plan and applicable arrangements need checking before responsibility is settled.

A plumber’s location findings can help that process, but a photo of the flooded bathroom does not establish ownership of the failed pipe. Keep the assessment and invoice scope clear, including who authorises urgent clearing and who can approve any separate repair.

How access changes the investigation

Available drainage access

Basement gates, locked cupboards, courtyard covers and parked vehicles can affect access. Supply the building contact’s details and explain any restrictions before the visit. Our Lower North Shore sewer blockage service selects a suitable entry point and equipment for the accessible installation.

What can be checked after flow returns

Where useful, a camera can help investigate roots, displaced joints or another recurring defect after the line is sufficiently clear. An inspection may be incomplete if debris, bends or damage prevent travel. Ask for the inspected section and limitations to be identified in the findings.

Keep a useful record for the building

Record when the first backup occurred, which units reported symptoms and what normal activity preceded it. Do not recreate the overflow to obtain evidence. Our guide to a coordinated strata drainage report explains how one clear account helps avoid conflicting messages.

After the visit, ask what was cleared, whether flow was checked and whether a defect still needs repair. Cleaning contaminated finishes and repairing drainage may require separate scopes. Confirm those boundaries so a successful clearing is not mistaken for completion of every recovery task.

When reporting a blocked drain in a strata building, identify the affected unit and whether neighbours have noticed symptoms. The location of the backup alone does not decide who pays.

Keep the backup location separate from responsibility

A ground-floor fixture may show the effects of a restriction elsewhere in connected drainage. Record upstairs use where known and coordinate access through strata. The investigation should locate the affected section before anyone assumes the lower unit caused it. Cost allocation then needs the relevant strata arrangements as well as the technical findings.
faqs: Does the ground-floor owner automatically pay?
No conclusion should be drawn from floor level alone. The location and ownership of the affected pipe, plus the relevant scheme arrangements, need to be established.
Can upstairs units have normal drainage during a shared blockage?
They may not show the same visible symptoms as a lower opening. Report what residents have already observed, but do not run extra water to test the shared line.
Should each unit keep testing its plumbing?
No. Further use can worsen a shared overflow. Coordinate advice through the building contact while the affected system is assessed.
Could an upstairs discharge affect a lower unit?
Yes. Connected drainage can make a lower fixture show symptoms of a restriction elsewhere. Location of the backup does not prove fault ownership.
Can a plumber's report help clarify responsibility?
It can identify the section and observed defect. Legal responsibility still depends on the property documents and applicable arrangements.
What if tenants discover the problem first?
Notify the managing agent or building emergency contact promptly, provide the evidence and follow the property's repair process.
Does urgent attendance guarantee reimbursement?
No. Keep records and notify the responsible contact, but do not assume that authorising work establishes who must pay.
What should the report say if access is incomplete?
Ask it to identify the sections inspected, access restrictions, remaining uncertainty and the next justified step.
What official guidance should the building check?
Use NSW Government strata repair guidance alongside the scheme's documents. Common-property responsibilities cannot be decided from the suburb or building type alone.
Does a shared symptom prove the owners corporation pays?
No. Establish the affected component and check the strata plan, by-laws and applicable responsibility before allocating costs.
check: What should the building contact collect?

The affected unit numbers and fixtures, first incident time, existing photos, access restrictions and an authorised decision-maker. Mark uncertain details as unknown and avoid sending residents into contaminated areas to investigate.
imageAlt: Plumber working with drain-clearing equipment beside a service vehicle
caption: A shared drainage investigation needs suitable access and coordination with the building’s contact.
introduction: A ground-floor unit can receive a backup from a restriction in shared drainage, even when the blockage did not start inside that unit. Wastewater may appear at a low connected fixture when it cannot flow away normally. Antons Blocked Drains Lower North Shore investigates the affected section before drawing conclusions about the cause or repair responsibility.
takeaways: The unit receiving the overflow is not necessarily where the blockage began.
Stop using affected fixtures and promptly alert the building contact.
Do not enter pits, open heavy covers or touch contaminated water.
Responsibility depends on the pipe and scheme information, not floor level alone.

conclusion: A ground-floor backup needs prompt coordination and a properly located diagnosis. Establish where the restriction sits before deciding what clearing, repair and follow-up the building needs.

title: Drain Work Through a Narrow Side Passage: What Affects Access and Equipment?
seoTitle: Narrow Access for Drain Clearing? Lower North Shore Guide
description: Planning drain work through a narrow side passage? Learn which access details affect equipment, hose routes and the scope of a Lower North Shore visit.
body:
Show the complete route from the street

A photograph of the open gate is a good start, but the difficult part may be farther along the house. An air-conditioning unit, low awning, raised step or sharp corner can restrict movement. Take a few wide photos from a safe position to show the full route.

Measure the narrowest clear width if you can do so safely and give the measurement in centimetres. Include the space left when the gate is fully open. Tell us about fragile surfaces, loose pavers and anything that cannot be moved. Do not remove equipment or fencing before the work plan is agreed.

Where is the actual drain access point?

The closest point to the blockage is not necessarily a suitable entry point for clearing equipment. A plumber needs to assess the available inspection opening, pipe direction and working space. A covered or buried opening may require further work before the drain can be investigated.

Point out known access locations in your photos without lifting heavy covers. If the only route crosses a neighbour’s property or a common area, explain that early. Permission and safe access need organising before attendance; a convenient shortcut is not automatically available for use.

Hoses, cameras and excavation machinery are different

Drain clearing and inspection

Some equipment can be operated with the vehicle positioned away from the drain opening, but hose reach, bends and safe routing still matter. Our Lower North Shore drain jetting service assesses the blockage and access before selecting a suitable approach.

A camera may help inspect accessible pipework, but it cannot guarantee passage through a complete obstruction. Ask whether inspection is planned before or after initial clearing and what happens if the opening cannot be safely reached. Avoid assuming that compact equipment removes every access limitation.

Repair work involving excavation

A route suitable for a hose may be unsuitable for an excavator or spoil removal. Hand work, alternate access or staged work may need discussion. The repair quote should explain those constraints rather than treating drain clearing and excavation as the same visit.

SafeWork NSW’s excavation guidance requires information about underground services before excavation begins. Tight access does not remove that need. Existing cables, water pipes and adjoining structures must be considered when planning any digging.

Prepare the property without overdoing it

  1. Send route photos and available measurements with the enquiry.
  2. Explain parking restrictions and the distance from a safe vehicle position.
  3. Secure pets and arrange access through locked gates.
  4. Ask which lightweight items should be moved before the visit.

Keep children and customers away from the proposed work route. For a shop or shared residence, discuss how pedestrian access will be maintained. Do not promise access through occupied rooms or neighbouring land without checking who can authorise it.

Ask the quote to state its access assumptions. If extra labour, lifting, surface protection or reinstatement is needed, clarify whether it is included. Clear information at booking gives the team a better chance of arriving with an appropriate plan and reduces avoidable surprises.

Send an access briefing before the visit

Photograph the passage safely and describe steps, tight turns, locked gates, parking distance and the inspection opening. Do not move heavy covers or alter structures yourself. Ask what equipment can reach the work area and what alternative access would involve. Clear access information helps distinguish preparation costs from the actual drain-clearing or inspection work.
faqs: Can you guarantee clearing from photos?
No. Photos help prepare, but the drain condition, entry point and safe setup need assessment. A suitable method can be confirmed once those details are understood.
Should I remove a fence panel first?
Wait for the access plan. Fence removal may be unnecessary and can affect security or neighbouring property. Agree on any changes and responsibilities before making them.
What measurements help assess a narrow passage?
Provide the narrowest clear width, steps, turns and gate openings, with safe photos. Equipment access needs more than the width at the entrance.
Can hoses always reach from street parking?
No. Distance, routing, elevation and equipment requirements matter. Describe the route before the visit rather than assuming reach.
Should I move heavy objects out of the passage?
Only clear items you can safely move. Discuss heavy equipment, unstable materials or structural obstructions with the attending team first.
Does a locked inspection area delay drain work?
It can. Arrange authorised access through the owner or building contact before attendance.
Can another inspection opening avoid restricted access?
Sometimes. The available openings and connected route need checking before an alternative approach can be confirmed.
Will limited access change the quote?
It may alter setup, equipment and the work sequence. Ask which access assumptions underpin the price.
Can CCTV help plan work through a narrow route?
It can provide evidence where access and visibility permit, but it cannot guarantee that all clearing or repair equipment will fit.
What should happen if the planned equipment cannot reach?
Ask for the limitation and options to be explained before extra work is authorised, including any alternative access or separate repair scope.
check: What photos will help with a narrow-access booking?

Send the street or driveway position, open gate, tightest section, steps and turns, and known drain access point. Include measurements where safe, and identify surfaces or equipment that must stay in place.
imageAlt: Technician beside a service vehicle fitted with drain-clearing equipment
caption: Vehicle positioning and the route to the drain access point both affect the work plan.
introduction: A narrow side passage does not automatically prevent drain clearing, but it can change the equipment, hose route and labour needed. Gate width is only one part of access. Steps, tight turns, drain entry points and a safe vehicle position all need checking before a method or price can be confirmed.
takeaways: Measure the tightest clear opening, not just the gate frame.
Describe steps, corners and the full route to the drain.
Jetting access and excavation access have different requirements.
Photos help plan a visit but cannot guarantee a method will fit.

seoTitle: Strata Drain Excavation Under a Courtyard: Approval Checks
description: Before approving courtyard drain excavation, strata needs clear fault evidence, responsibility checks, an access plan and a defined reinstatement scope.
imageAlt: Excavated drain beneath a paved area with inspection equipment nearby
caption: A courtyard repair scope should explain the drainage work and how the disturbed surface will be restored.
introduction: Before approving excavation of a shared drain under a courtyard, strata needs evidence of the fault, a confirmed repair scope, responsibility checks and a plan for access and reinstatement. A quote saying only “dig and repair drain” leaves too many decisions unresolved for owners and residents.
takeaways: Confirm the affected pipe and the evidence supporting excavation.
Check the strata plan and by-laws before assigning responsibility.
Include resident access, service interruptions and surface restoration.
Name the person authorised to approve changes during the work.
body:
Start with a finding the committee can understand

A useful proposal connects the symptom to the recommended work. It should identify the affected line, explain the observed defect and state how the location was established. Where camera footage is available, ask for relevant images and a plain-English explanation, not just a long video file.

Also record the limits of the investigation. If a section could not be reached or viewed clearly, that uncertainty belongs in the proposal. A blockage returning after clearing does not by itself prove that the whole courtyard drain needs replacement.

Confirm responsibility and authority

The fact that a drain runs under a private-use courtyard does not settle who must arrange or pay for repairs. The NSW Government’s strata repair guidance distinguishes common-property responsibilities from an owner’s responsibilities and directs owners to check plans and by-laws where the position is unclear.

Ask the strata manager to establish the relevant authority before approving the work. Keep the decision, quote version and any conditions together. This article is a practical checklist for the repair proposal; the scheme’s specific legal position needs to be resolved through its records and appropriate advice.

Make the excavation scope specific

For strata drain repairs on the Lower North Shore, ask for a description of the intended opening, pipe repair and completion checks. The proposal should explain why excavation is recommended and what reasonable alternatives have been considered for the actual defect.

Agree what happens if the finding changes

Buried conditions can differ from what is visible during investigation. Nominate who can approve a variation, how the finding will be documented and when residents will be updated. A contractor should not have to work through a long chain of informal messages to get a clear instruction.

Plan for the courtyard while work is under way

Residents need to know which areas will be unavailable and how they will enter and leave safely. The plan should address:

  • Access through units, gates or common corridors.
  • Protection of finishes along the equipment route.
  • Any expected interruption to drainage use.
  • Barriers, pets, children and arrangements outside working hours.

Underground service information must also be considered before digging. SafeWork NSW explains the requirement to obtain essential service information. A drain location is not a complete map of everything under the courtyard.

Specify the finish as well as the pipe

Ask who will lift and store reusable pavers, remove spoil, backfill and reinstate the surface. If waterproofing, a slab or a specialist finish could be affected, establish the appropriate trade and scope before work starts. Matching old finishes may need separate discussion.

Compare quotes against the same brief. One may include only the pipe repair while another includes surface restoration and testing. Treat differences in access assumptions and exclusions as questions to resolve, rather than choosing solely on the total price.

Close out the repair with useful records

Request a record of the repaired section, completion checks and any remaining recommendations. Keep relevant photos, updated location information and the final invoice with the strata records. That gives the next committee or manager a practical history if drainage work is needed again.
check: Is the proposal ready for approval?

Check for fault evidence, responsibility, exact work, resident access, reinstatement and a variation contact. If any item is missing, resolve it with the manager and contractor before approving non-urgent excavation.
faqs: Is a drain under my courtyard automatically my responsibility?
No. Location alone is not enough. Ask the manager to check the strata plan, by-laws and the affected plumbing.
Does camera footage prove excavation is necessary?
It may support the recommendation, but ask which defect is visible, how it was located and why the proposed repair suits it.
What if the camera could not inspect the whole pipe?
The proposal should state the uninspected section and uncertainty. It should not present unseen pipe as confirmed damage.
Can one owner approve work on a shared drain?
Have the strata manager confirm the authority required for the scope. Do not assume an individual instruction covers common-property work.
Should all quotes include courtyard restoration?
Compare them on the same basis. Ask each contractor to identify restoration work, exclusions and any separate specialist trade.
Who informs residents about restricted access?
Agree this with the strata manager and contractor before work starts, including a contact for changed timings or interruptions.
What should happen if more damage is uncovered?
Document the finding and obtain approval through the nominated contact for the changed scope, subject to necessary immediate safety measures.
Will the existing pavers be reused?
Ask what condition and availability assumptions the quote makes. Reuse or an exact match cannot be presumed.
Can urgent containment happen before the full repair is approved?
Notify the manager promptly and follow the scheme’s urgent repair process. Separate immediate safety or containment needs from the permanent repair proposal.
What documents should strata retain afterwards?
Keep the approved scope, variations, relevant photos, completion findings and any updated pipe location information.
conclusion: A clear approval package links the confirmed drainage problem to the repair, access and restoration plan. Resolve responsibilities and decision-making before the courtyard is opened.
